lanesBuilt: EffectGrant.grantsCreatureTraits — a creature trait belonging to ONE BRANCH of a choice. Collected by applyAlwaysOn (src/rules/build.ts) into the new Character.chosenCreatureTraits, which keeps the granting record's NAME (chosenEffects is a merged DefenseGrants bag the breakdown labels 'Your chosen effect', which cannot answer 'which feat made me an azata'). Carries Swimming Animal's aquatic branch, Deity (Champion)'s holy/unholy/none, and Elemental Apotheosis' six elements.

grantsCreatureTraitFromChoice on DefenseGrants — names the record's own choice flag; the ANSWER is the trait. Resolved in buildCharacter (not creatureTraitsOf) because a class feature's and a heritage's answers live in BuildState.featChoices, which the built Character does not carry — doing it in one place stops the three carriers drifting into 'works on feats, silently inert on features'. Carries Celestial Form, Fiendish Form (both allowCustom: the printed lists say 'for example' / 'such as') and Celestial Rebirth (closed four, whose picker had zero readers in src/).

ModeDef.creatureTraits — a trait that is only true while something is running. Read from Character.activeModes by creatureTraitsOf, attributed to the mode. Carries Worm Form's 'while in this form' animal trait (moved onto its two existing battle-form modes) and a new predefined, feat-gated mode fey-life-revived for Fey Life's post-death fey trait.
creatureTraitsOf (src/rules/derive.ts) now folds four sources instead of two: ancestry, record-level grantsCreatureTraits, Character.chosenCreatureTraits, and active modes' creatureTraits.

InnateSpellGrant.minLevel — a grant that arrives on a LEVEL LADDER ("At 10th level, you can also cast Seal Fate, and at 12th level, Inevitable Disaster"). The type had no availability gate at all, which is why Accursed Magic handed an 8th-level taker all three spells and the sibling Lion's Magic resolved the same sentence by DROPPING its 12th-level spell. Below minLevel the grant is dropped before the innate dedupe claims the id, and so is any spellNotes clause the same record writes about that spell — a rider on a spell the feat does not yet grant is worse than none. src/rules/types.ts (InnateSpellGrant), src/rules/build.ts innate filter + the spellNotes loop.

ContentBase.voidHealingSpellSwap — the spell a record grants DEPENDS ON THE CHARACTER: Mortal Herald Dedication prints "**Special** If you have void healing, you instead cast Harm." InnateSpellGrant has no predicate, so a dhampir was granted Heal and all four riders (self-only, 1-action gets the 2-action benefit, auto-heighten, free action at 0 HP) were filed on it; authoring Harm instead would have been equally wrong for everyone else. Applied at build time to the grant AND to the record's own note, whose text has the spell's name substituted (word-boundary, case-sensitive, so "Heal" never eats "healing"). hasVoidHealing mirrors derive.ts's negativeHealing rule exactly, invested-only for items, so the sheet cannot give two answers to one question. Honoured on the always-on paths only; a test pins that exactly one record carries it and that it is not authored inside effectChoices, where it would be resolved and dropped in silence.

DegreeShift.shift gained `critFailToSuccess` (+ DEGREE_SHIFT_TEXT "a critical failure is a success instead" / DEGREE_SHIFT_SHORT "crit fail → success"), in src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts. Four records print "when you roll a failure OR CRITICAL FAILURE … you get a success instead" and were authored `failToSuccess` alone. Both values a reader reaches for are wrong in opposite directions: `failToSuccess` alone tells a player who has just critically failed the rule misses them, and `oneBetter` both understates the crit failure (→ failure, not success) and invents a success → critical success upgrade none of the four grants. Paired with `failToSuccess`, one entry per rung, the shape every other two-degree record uses.

WITHDRAWN in scripts/apply-degree-shifts.mjs — a way to UNSAY a value the table authored once. Deleting a key only stops the script writing; the old value stays in public/core.json AND in the overlay row that survives `npm run data`, so a silent removal leaves the defect shipped. WITHDRAWN deletes the field from both, refuses a key that is also in AUTHORED, and prints what it removed with why. Used for the two doctrine umbrellas (classFeatures/battle-creed, classFeatures/warpriest), whose clause was structurally ungateable: ownedFeatureIds adds a chosen subclass id with no level check and DegreeShift has no level field.

DegreeShift.savesFromChoice got its READER. The field was declared in src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts with a doc comment pointing at `resolveChoiceSaves` (explain.ts) — which had never been written, so the field was write-only and path-to-perfection had to keep saying saves:['all']. Built CHOICE_SAVE_ANSWERS + resolveChoiceSaves in src/rules/explain.ts and wired it into the degreeShifts fan-out in authoredSituational; an unanswered pick now stars nothing rather than everything.

Character.pathToPerfection (src/rules/types.ts) — the monk's save picks now travel from BuildState onto the built Character. They could not be recovered from the numbers: buildFromCharacter re-derives them by reading which saves are master/legendary and its own comment calls the order "approximate", which is fine for reopening the builder and useless for naming ONE of three rows. buildCharacter writes the answers (gated on classId/classId2 === 'monk'), and buildFromCharacter now prefers the stored answers over its rank-reading fallback, so a save-and-reopen round trip can no longer move the star to the other row.

scripts/apply-degree-shifts.mjs — the `e()` shorthand gained `svPick`, so the authoring table can express "the save the player chose" instead of being forced to pick between a wrong track and ['all'].

test/degree-shifts.test.ts — the shipped invariant "every action a shift names exists" built its known-id set from content.actions alone, which under-approximates the id space the two renderers actually key off (MainTab slugifies ACTIVITIES, StatDetailModal slugifies SKILL_ACTIONS). Battle Medicine is a curated row on both and has no content.actions record, so a CORRECT mark on it read as a mark on nothing. Widened to the union. Same test file: the surface counter now counts savesFromChoice as a surface, and a new test forbids setting savesFromChoice and saves together.

ReachRider.combinesWithSize + ReachRider.fromSize (src/rules/types.ts) with the combination resolved in strikeReaches (src/rules/derive.ts) — Giant's Lunge's third clause ("it does combine with abilities that increase your reach due to increased size") could not be expressed: a stated `feet` wins over `add` by design, so a raging giant-instinct barbarian holding Giant's Lunge AND Giant's Stature saw two separate 10-ft rows and never the 15 ft the rule gives. Re-authoring as `add: 5` (the obvious 'fix') would have been wrong for any character whose reach is not 5, so the field learned to say the sentence instead. Each size rider combines SEPARATELY, never summed — a creature is one size, and Titan's Stature is explicitly an alternative to Giant's Stature.

scripts/apply-special-statistics.mjs now throws when any deviant classification carrying a specialStatistic has no feat granting it — the reachability assumption its own header stated in prose is now a check that fails.
disputed: None refused. Two remedies were changed rather than the findings: (1) heritages/cliffscale-lizardfolk — the finding proposed dropping only the leading "while not wearing footwear, " and keeping "(your hands stay free)". Keeping it re-asserts the footwear-gated hands-free claim unconditionally, which is the same over-promise moved one clause along; the whole parenthetical went and the `when` is now "on an Athletics check to Climb". The hands-free rule keeps its real footwear condition as the Climb RecordMarker in situationalBonuses.ts, which the new test asserts is still there. (2) The single `questionable` entry in this half (feats/commitment-to-protection skills `lore` → `lore:warfare`) I judged CORRECT and fixed: the authoring script's own comment ten lines from the offending row states the rule for Explosive Entry — "a bare `lore` would star every Lore the character has for a feat that only ever touches this one" — and targetMatches confirms bare `lore` matches every `lore:*` row while the feat names Warfare Lore three times and is prerequisite-gated on it.

stillWrong: classFeatures/deity-champion — the per-branch trait is right, but it hangs off a SECOND sanctification question. 261 deity records already carry an effectChoices entry with id 'sanctification' (e.g. deities/maat offers holy/none only), and its answer is what sanctificationOf() reads (src/rules/derive.ts:1194, off c.effectPicks). The fix's picker is classFeatures/deity-champion.choice, whose answer lands in build.featChoices['feature:deity-champion'] and NEVER reaches effectPicks (only resolvePick pushes there — src/rules/build.ts:3515). Three consequences: (a) a champion is asked the same question twice and the two answers can disagree; (b) the class-feature picker always offers holy/unholy/none with no choiceOptionLimits targeting it, so a champion of Maat can pick unholy — the text says "If you 'can be' holy or unholy according to your deity's sanctification entry, you make that choice" and "If the deity lists 'none,' you can choose only options that don't require the holy or unholy trait"; (c) picking holy on the class feature does not widen addIfSanctified menus, because sanctificationOf() still returns null. The faithful carrier is grant.grantsCreatureTraits on the deity's own sanctification options (currently 0 of 522 such options carry a grant).

feats/elemental-apotheosis — ['elemental'] plus a per-element trait is correct, but the text says "the trait of YOUR CHOSEN element", i.e. the element already chosen as a kineticist (the prerequisite is literally "exactly one kinetic element"). The effectChoices picker offers all six elements with no binding to kineticistElements(build, level) (src/rules/build.ts:4880) and no choiceOptionLimits targets it, so a fire kineticist can answer 'wood' and acquire the wood creature trait plus a 30-ft climb Speed. Before this fix the same picker only moved Speeds; the fix made an unconstrained answer identity-defining.

feats/worm-form — the animal trait moved correctly onto modes/worm-form-purple-worm and modes/worm-form-hybrid, but there is a SECOND carrier for the same form: core.stances['worm-form'] (form: true), toggled via c.activeStance and read by activeStanceDef(). creatureTraitsOf (src/rules/derive.ts:2225) reads activeModes only, never activeStance, and the stance record has no creatureTraits field — its note merely says "(animal trait)" as prose. A worm caller who enters the form through the stance/form control gets its darkvision and none of its animal trait.

heritages/swimming-animal — the aquatic-trait defect is fixed, but the fix rewrote the whole effectChoices array and left one clause of the same sentence unimplemented. The water-dwelling label it wrote reads "swim Speed 20 ft, land Speed 20 ft" while its grant is only { speeds: { swim: 20 } }; the text says "You have a swim Speed of 20 feet, and if you can move on land, you have base Speed of 20 feet." ancestries/awakened-animal has speed { land: 5 }, so the label promises 20 and the sheet derives 5. (The gap predates this fix, but it sits inside the value this fix replaced.)

NOT A FAILED FIX — a residual gap found while re-reading. feats/pact-of-eldritch-eyes: the corrected field (innateSpells, now usesPerDay 1 + usesPer 'hour') is CORRECT against 'once per hour'. But the same sentence also prints 'using the higher of your class DC and your spell DC to determine the DC', and the record still carries no spellNotes at all. Its identical twin feats/pact-of-fey-glamour — corrected in the same script, same sentence shape — DOES author that clause as a spellNote. Pre-existing, not introduced by this fix. Systemic: 6 innate-granting feats whose text names a DC choice carry no note (animal-magic, innocent-butterfly, dominating-gaze, tengu-feather-fan, kaijus-footfalls, pact-of-eldritch-eyes) against 8 that do.

NOT A FAILED FIX — a residual gap. feats/vellumis-excision: the correction is right (innateSpells removed; spellListAdditions {as:'repertoire', entryId:'halcyon-speaker-dedication-casting'} + spellSlotBonus {byRank:{6:1}}), and I verified in the engine that the slot lands at level 16 via build.ts:4329-4334 (which CREATES the rank, two levels before the archetype would) and stacks to base+1 at level 18. But the record's printed Special clause — 'If you have the Halcyon Spellcasting Sage feat, you treat the field of life halcyon spell gained from this feat as a signature spell' — is still unauthored. The confirming agent named this clause as collateral damage of the mis-filing, so fixing the surface was a precondition for it; no signature-spell lane exists for a granted repertoire spell (types.ts has `signature?: string[]` on the entry only), so it needs a new lane, not a value.

classFeatures/third-path-to-perfection — the flagged sub-field (`when`) IS fixed and now names both sources ("on the save you chose for Third Path to Perfection, from those you selected for path to perfection or second path to perfection"), but the entry still carries `saves: ["all"]` while the printed text reads "When you roll a critical failure on THE CHOSEN TYPE OF SAVE, you get a failure instead." A monk who picked Reflex at 15th is told Fortitude and Will also turn critical failures into failures — the exact defect the same pass corrected on its two siblings. The lane now exists and can say it: path-to-perfection got `savesFromChoice: 'pathToPerfection:0'` and second-path-to-perfection got `:1`, and index 2 is the Third Path legendary pick, stored and recovered (src/rules/build.ts:3015 applies picks[2] at level 15; build.ts:5475 round-trips all three; resolveChoiceSaves in src/rules/explain.ts:290 reads it). The one-line fix is `{ svPick: 'pathToPerfection:2' }` in place of `{ sv: ALL }` at scripts/apply-degree-shifts.mjs:169, then re-run so core.json and effect-backfill.json follow.

classFeatures/third-path-to-perfection — the `when` half of the finding is fixed ("on the save you chose for Third Path to Perfection, from those you selected for path to perfection or second path to perfection"), but the entry still carries saves:["all"], so all three save rows star while the trigger names one chosen save. Its two siblings were converted in this same batch (path-to-perfection → savesFromChoice "pathToPerfection:0", second-path-to-perfection → ":1"); Character.pathToPerfection index [2] is documented (src/rules/types.ts:4015) and populated (src/rules/build.ts:5475) as the 15th-level legendary pick, so savesFromChoice "pathToPerfection:2" is available. overCorrected: feats/fey-life — the new modes/fey-life-revived carries duration: "permanent — once you have died the first time". ModeDef.duration is documented in src/rules/types.ts as "The printed duration", and all 466 other uses are short printed phrases ("1 day", "10 minutes", "until the start of your next turn"). Nothing in the feat's text says "permanent". It renders through src/sheet/ModeDetailModal.tsx:25 as "Lasts permanent — once you have died the first time." and onto the VitalsRail pill (src/sheet/VitalsRail.tsx:1117) in full. The mode's own note already carries the timing correctly; the duration field should be dropped or reduced to something printed.

heritages/swimming-animal — the water-dwelling option's new note asserts "…so you do NOT gain the aquatic trait, which would mean breathing water and not air." The printed text never states this; it is the app's (sound) inference from the aquatic branch's definition, written in the second person into a player-facing field as though it were rules text. Low severity and defensible, but it is app reasoning presented as the record's own content — the aquatic branch's note, by contrast, is a verbatim quote of the printed sentence.

feats/crystal-keeper-dedication — the flagged defect is fixed correctly (skills ["arcana","occultism","religion","society"] added to both entries), but the `when` was ALSO rewritten, from "when you Decipher Writing" to "when you Decipher Writing by meditating before a crystal", which the shift sentence does not say. The pristine AoN text (C:/wonderers guide/aon-2e-archive/data/by-category/feat/feat-1146.json) puts the crystal proviso on the skill-substitution sentence only: "You can use Arcana, Occultism, Religion, or Society to Decipher Writing by meditating before a crystal, regardless of the type of writing. When you Decipher Writing and roll a critical failure, you get a failure instead, and when you Decipher Writing and roll a success, you get a critical success instead." This is the mirror image of heritages/cliffscale-lizardfolk, where THIS SAME BATCH correctly REMOVED an adjacent-sentence proviso ("while not wearing footwear") from a shift's `when` on exactly that reasoning. As it now reads, a crystal keeper who Deciphers Writing without a crystal in front of them is told the upgrade does not apply. Restore the pre-fix `when` ("when you Decipher Writing") and keep the new skills; scripts/apply-degree-shifts.mjs:369-372.

feats/crystal-keeper-dedication — the skills half of the fix is right (arcana/occultism/religion/society), but the `when` gained "by meditating before a crystal", which the shift clause does not say. Printed text (verified against the AoN archive, feat-1146.json): the crystal qualifies the FIRST sentence ("You can use Arcana, Occultism, Religion, or Society to Decipher Writing by meditating before a crystal"); the shift sentence is unqualified — "When you Decipher Writing and roll a critical failure, you get a failure instead, and when you Decipher Writing and roll a success, you get a critical success instead." Since `when` prints verbatim in the note, a player deciphering writing without a crystal is told the upgrade does not reach them. Same shape as heritages/cliffscale-lizardfolk, where this batch correctly REMOVED the identical borrowed qualifier ("while not wearing footwear"). scripts/apply-degree-shifts.mjs line 369.
